cover.title: 5 niche ways to find which european country quits your checkout first

inner.title: split the funnel by country
inner.body: ga4 funnel exploration lets you break every step down by a dimension and compare up to four segments. an average hides it, so build one segment per country and see who stops where.

inner.title: read the next action
inner.body: the top 5 next actions card shows what people do after each step, and a (no next action) entry can signal a drop-off. if germany leaves at payment and the netherlands doesn't, you know which page to open.

inner.title: offer the local bank
inner.body: stripe lists ideal as a netherlands method and bancontact as a belgium method, and a customer has 1 hour to approve a bancontact payment. if your checkout shows only cards, dutch and belgian buyers pay a way they don't use.

inner.title: show the vat price early
inner.body: baymard-based figures put extra costs as the top reason for leaving at 48%. under the eu price indication directive prices must include vat, and adding it silently at checkout is non-compliant.

inner.title: kill the forced account
inner.body: 26% of shoppers left because they had to create an account, and the average cart abandonment rate across 50 studies is 70.22%. every country sees the same wall, so test guest checkout first.
